name: wordcount_container_merge
task: This project counts word frequencies in a synthetic text corpus, split across multiple translation units: include/corpus.h + src/corpus.cpp (a deterministic corpus generator with a skewed word distribution), include/tokenizer.h + src/tokenizer.cpp (split_words()), include/word_count.h + src/word_count.cpp (serial and OpenMP-parallel word counting into a std::unordered_map<std::string, long long>, plus top_k() and total_words() helpers), and src/main.cpp (the profiling entry point). count_words_parallel() in src/word_count.cpp parallelizes the loop over lines with '#pragma omp parallel for', but every thread inserts into and increments the same shared std::unordered_map. Standard containers are not thread-safe: concurrent operator[] calls race on the bucket array, node allocation and rehashing, so increments are lost, entries can be dropped or duplicated, and the program may crash or hang. Fix count_words_parallel() so it returns exactly the same map as count_words_serial() for any corpus and any number of threads, while keeping the loop over lines parallelized with OpenMP (do not simply remove the pragma or serialize the loop; for example give every thread its own WordCounts and merge them after the parallel loop, or merge inside an '#pragma omp critical' section, or protect each update). Do not change any function signature or the WordCounts type declared in include/word_count.h, include/corpus.h or include/tokenizer.h.
notes: build_command compiles the profiling entry point at build/app (src/main.cpp -> corpus.cpp, tokenizer.cpp, word_count.cpp). This binary must be built and then executed via run_command to drive DiscoPoP's instrumentation and produce its dynamic profiling output, including dynamic_dependencies, over the parallel loop over lines in count_words_parallel(). test_command builds and runs a separate correctness harness at build/run_tests (from tests/test_main.cpp); it is independent of the profiling binary and should not be used as the DiscoPoP execution target. Both binaries link the same corpus.cpp, tokenizer.cpp, word_count.cpp object files, so no separate CMake/Meson/etc. configuration is required — plain 'make' is sufficient to build, run, and test.
